Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

knock out verb

in boxing

also knockout, knock someone out

classical

Liv. 8.6: impactus ita est saxō, ut sōpīrētur, he was stunned (Lewis & Short: “became unconscious or senseless”)

sōpiō, sōpīre, sōpīvī, sōpītum

verb, fourth conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

knock senseless, stun

To put to sleep, and so to knock someone senseless: the boxer who is knocked out is sōpītus.

Other words

  • cerebrum alicui dīminuere

    also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 4.2.32: cerebrum tibi (Lewis & Short s.v. dīminuō); Traupman 46

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

    Literally “to smash someone’s skull”: in comedy a threat of violence (Plaut. Men. 2.2.30 caput hominī), not of stunning. Traupman uses it for a knockout in boxing.

  • cōnsternō, cōnsternere, cōnstrāvī, cōnstrātum — knock down, lay flat

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 40.45.3: tempestās in Capitōliō aliquot signa cōnstrāvit, “throw down, prostrate (very rare)” (Lewis & Short); Traupman 336 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • prōflīgō, prōflīgāre, prōflīgāvī, prōflīgātum — strike down, overthrow

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 336 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

See also boxing, punch.
